title: The same State scorecard for the ten largest areas
question: How does San Francisco's record on the State homelessness grant compare with the other large cities and counties in the same State files?
finding: Among the ten largest areas San Francisco slid from near the top to the bottom of the State's scorecard. It was marked as progressing on 6, 4 and 1 of seven measures for rounds 4, 5 and 6, against a middle figure of 4.5, 4 and 2: 1 area(s) did better and 6 worse in round 4, 3 area(s) did better and 4 worse in round 5, 8 area(s) did better and 0 worse in round 6. 1 of the 9 areas with a round 4 target for people sleeping outside reached it (Sacramento City & County); San Francisco was 177 over its target of 4,177, a cut of 5% from its 2022 count where the middle target among these areas was a cut of 12%.
how: The ten areas with the most people reached by homeless services in 2025, from the State housing department's tracker. Measures met are the department's own count of "Progress" marks out of seven for each round, and "passed" is its column for whether enough were met. The unsheltered columns set the target each area chose for 2025 in round 4 against the 2025 figure in the tracker.
limits: Areas are the planning areas the State file calls Continuums of Care, and they differ greatly in size, as the second column shows. Each area chose its own target, so reaching a modest target and missing an ambitious one are not comparable. The 2025 unsheltered figure is the latest count each area had, often taken in 2024. The marks compare an area with its own past, not with others.
